constraints.description: Applications must be made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector.
The standard duration of European Postdoctoral Fellowships must be between 12 and 24 months.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships require an outgoing phase of minimum 12 and maximum 24 months in a non-associated Third Country and a mandatory 12-month return phase to a host organisation in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

For European Postdoctoral Fellowships, secondments cannot exceed half of the requested duration of the action (excluding any additional period for a non-academic placement) and must be in line with project objectives.

For Global Postdoctoral Fellowships, optional secondments are permitted for up to half of the outgoing phase; a maximum of three months of such secondments can be spent at the beneficiary at the start of the project.
Secondments cannot take place during the mandatory twelve-month return period to the host organisation in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

Non-academic sector placements may provide an additional period of up to six months at the end of the project, at an organisation from the non-academic sector established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
constraints.source_section: Scope - Placements in the non-academic sector

constraints.description: For researchers recruited in the non-academic sector, the non-academic placement must be implemented at a different non-academic host organisation established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
constraints.source_section: Scope - Placements in the non-academic sector

constraints.description: The request for a non-academic placement must be an integral part of the proposal, explaining the added value for the project and for the career development of the researcher, and is subject to evaluation.
constraints.source_section: Scope - Placements in the non-academic sector

constraints.description: If a non-academic placement does not meet requirements (e.g. takes place in an academic organisation or in a Third Country), the proposal is evaluated without taking into account the placement, which may affect the final score.
constraints.source_section: Scope - Placements in the non-academic sector

constraints.description: Training activities must integrate key transferable skills and competences common to all fields, including digital ones (e.g. generative AI), and foster the culture of Open Science, knowledge valorisation, and good scientific conduct including research integrity.

Training activities must prepare fellows for increased research collaboration and information-sharing made possible by new digital technologies (e.g. collaborative tools, open access, FAIR data management, societal engagement, citizen science).

A Career Development Plan must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher, comprising research objectives, training and career needs, transferable skills, teaching, publications planning, and open science engagement. It must be submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action.
Specific eligibility conditions apply to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships in the research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme.
ERA Fellowships implemented through Work Programme Annex 11 provide specific support to researchers undertaking fellowships in widening countries.
Proposal page limits and layout are described in Part B of the Application Form available in the Submission System and in Annex A and Annex E of the Horizon Europe Work Programme General Annexes.
The call operates under a single-stage submission model with a deadline of 2026-09-09.
Budget regime for this instrument is unit_cost; no per-project maximum EU contribution is stated in the call extract documents.
constraints.inference_note: The call slice records max_contribution as 0.0, indicating no stated per-project ceiling. The selected_call.json confirms budget_regime as unit_cost. The inference is that individual fellowship cost is governed by unit rates (published in the MSCA WP) rather than a call-level cap per project.
